Rashi on Zevachim 11a:20:1.hebrew: אמרו דבר אחד: that Rabbi Eliezer also disqualifies other offerings slaughtered for the sake of a Pesach offering at its designated time, or for the sake of a ḥatat offering all year round, and Rabbi Yoḥanan derives this from a baraita below.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:10:1.hebrew: ומדסיפא - הבכור והמעשר ששחטן לשם שלמים כשרים ואין מרצין, אם כן רישא — קדשים קלים ששחטן לשם קדשי קדשים — נמי כשרין ואין מרצין קאמר:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:10:1.english: And since in the latter clause - a firstborn or a tithe [animal] that one slaughtered for the sake of peace-offerings are fit but do not propitiate, [it follows that] the former clause — lesser-sanctity offerings that one slaughtered for the sake of the most sacred offerings — likewise states that they are fit but do not propitiate.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:11:1.hebrew: הא כדאיתא כו' - "כשרין" דקתני גבי בכור, כשרין למילתייהו קאמר; [וכשרים נמי דקתני גבי קדשי קדשים, למילתייהו קאמר] ואפי' לרצות לשם חובה:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:11:1.english: This is as it is, etc. - The word "valid" that is taught regarding the firstborn means valid for their own purposes. [And "valid" as well that is taught regarding offerings of the most sacred order means valid for their own purposes,] and even to propitiate for the sake of an obligation.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:12:1.hebrew: אלא מאי קמשמע לן - האי דנקט הבכור והמעשר, אי לאו לגלויי עלה דרישא נקט לה, ולמימר דכשרין ואין מרצין קאמר:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:12:1.english: Rather, what does it teach us - That the Mishnah mentioned the firstborn and the animal tithe — if not to reveal something about the first clause, it would not have mentioned them; and it means to say that they are fit but do not propitiate.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:12:2.hebrew: גבוה ונמוך קמשמע לן - בתמיה: וכי אתא לפרושי לן היכי דמי נמוך לשם גבוה?
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:12:2.english: Higher and lower is it teaching us? - [This is said] as a rhetorical question: Did [the latter clause] come to explain to us what constitutes a lower [offering slaughtered] for the sake of a higher one?

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:12:3.english: We learned - in the first clause of the matter.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:12:4.hebrew: הא נמי תנינא - לקמן בפרק כל התדיר (זבחים דף פט.) דבכור נמוך משלמים:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:12:4.english: This too we learned - Later, in the chapter [beginning] "Kol HaTadir" (Zevachim 89a), [it is taught] that a firstborn is lower [in sanctity] than peace offerings.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:14:1.hebrew: שלמים קודמין את הבכור - אם שניהם עומדים לישחט בעזרה ולהקריב:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:14:1.english: A peace offering precedes the firstborn - If both of them are standing to be slaughtered in the Temple courtyard and to be offered.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:14:2.hebrew: שהן טעונים מתן ארבע - שתי מתנות שהן ארבע, ובכור במתנה אחת, כדתנן באיזהו מקומן (לקמן זבחים נו:). סמיכה ונסכים ליתנהו בבכור, כדילפינן במנחות בפרק שתי מדות (מנחות דף צ:):
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:14:2.english: That they require placement of four - Two placements that are [effectively] four [on the four sides of the altar], whereas the firstborn [requires] one placement, as we learned in the chapter "Eizehu Mekoman" (below, Zevachim 56b). Placing hands and libations do not apply to the firstborn, as we derive in Menachot, in the chapter "Shtei Midot" (Menachot 90b).

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:15:1.hebrew: הא עיקר - שנשנית תחילה, לצורך לאשמועינן גבי פסול שלא לשמו דאיכא בקדשים קלים גבוה ונמוך:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:15:1.english: The primary [mention] - That was taught first, for the purpose of teaching us, with regard to the disqualification of [offering] not for its own sake, that among the lesser sacred offerings there is [a distinction between] high and low.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:15:2.hebrew: ההיא - דכל התדיר מתניתין אגררא נסבה, ששנה שם את הקודמים זה לזה, ונקט נמי האי בהדייהו, אע"ג דכבר תנייה הכא:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:15:2.english: That - The mishna of "whichever is more frequent" cites it incidentally, for it taught there the offerings that take precedence over one another, and it also included this one (the distinction) along with them, even though it had already been taught here.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:16:1.hebrew: רבי יהושע מכשיר - דפסח בשאר ימות השנה חשיב ליה:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:16:1.english: Rabbi Yehoshua deems it fit - For he considers it [like] a Paschal offering [slaughtered] during the rest of the days of the year.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:16:2.hebrew: בן בתירא פוסל - בגמרא מפרש להו:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:16:2.english: Ben Beteira deems it unfit - The Gemara explains them.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:17:1.hebrew: שבעים ושנים זקן - בגמרא מפרש אמאי לא תנא זקנים:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:17:1.english: Seventy-two elders - The Gemara explains why [the Tanna] did not teach "elders" [in the plural form].

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:17:2.hebrew: כל הזבחים הנאכלין - אבל עולה לא:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:17:2.english: All the offerings that are eaten - But a burnt offering is not [included].

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:17:3.hebrew: לא הוסיף בן עזאי - על דברי חכמים לפסול את הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן חוץ מפסח ומחטאת, אלא העולה:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:17:3.english: Ben Azzai added nothing - to the words of the Sages, who disqualify [offerings slaughtered not for their own sake] other than the Paschal offering and the sin offering, except the burnt offering. [He added only the burnt offering to the list of those that do not satisfy the owner's obligation.]

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:18:1.hebrew: מכשיר היה בן בתירא בפסח ששחטו שחרית לשמו - והוה ליה זמנו, לפיכך פסול שלא לשמו, כדאמר: פסח בזמנו שלא לשמו פסול:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:18:1.english: Ben Beteira would deem fit a Paschal offering that one slaughtered in the morning for its own sake - For it is then in its [proper] time, and therefore [if slaughtered] not for its own sake it is invalid, as [the Mishnah] stated: A Paschal offering in its time [slaughtered] not for its own sake is invalid.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:18:2.hebrew: בן בתירא פוסל - בגמרא מפרש להו.:אבדעקמוןרו
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:18:2.english: Ben Beteira deems it unfit - The Gemara explains his reasoning.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:19:1.hebrew: ומאי כאילו - נשחט בין הערבים? והאמרת דכולא יומא בין הערבים קרי ליה, מדקמכשרת ליה שחרית — וקרא כתיב ״בין הערבים״! אלמא סבירא ליה ״בין ערב של אמש לערב של אחריו״, כדמפרשינן ליה לקמיה — דהיינו משעלה השחר, שפסק ליל של אמש, עד שתשקע החמה. ומאי ״כאילו״? הא הוא גופיה ״בין הערבים״:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:19:1.english: And what [is meant by] "as though" - [As though] it were slaughtered "between the evenings"? But you said that the whole day is called "between the evenings," since you deem it valid in the morning, and the verse states "between the evenings"! Evidently he holds that it means between the evening of last night and the evening of the following one, as we explain below — that is, from when dawn rises, when last night ended, until the sun sets. So what [is meant by] "as though"? It itself is [actually] "between the evenings"!

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:1:1.hebrew: אמר לו רבי יהושע מצינו מותר חטאת בא עולה - כדתניא בתמורה (דף כג:) זה מדרש דרש יהוידע הכהן: כל דבר שבא ממותר חטאת וממותר אשם, ילקח בהן עולה לקיץ המזבח. והיכי דמי מותר חטאת? כגון הפריש מעות לחטאתו וניתותרו, אי נמי מפריש שתי חטאות לאחריות, דקי"ל בתמורה (דף כד.) מתכפר באחת מהן, והשניה תרעה:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:1:1.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: We find that a leftover sin offering is brought as a burnt offering - As it was taught in Temurah (23b): This is the teaching that Yehoyada the Priest taught: "Anything that comes from the leftovers of a sin offering or from the leftovers of a guilt offering, a burnt offering is bought with them, as a 'summer fruit' for the altar." And what is a case of a leftover sin offering? For example, one who set aside money for his sin offering and some was left over; or alternatively, one who set aside two sin offerings as a safeguard, for we hold in Temurah (24a) that he achieves atonement with one of them, and the second is left to graze:

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:21:1.hebrew: ליפלגו בלשמו - ולימא מתניתין [פסח ששחטו בי"ד שחרית] ר' יהושע פוסל ובן בתירא מכשיר:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:21:1.english: Let them disagree about [a Paschal offering slaughtered] for its own sake - And let [the mishna] say: [A Paschal offering that one slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth] — Rabbi Yehoshua deems it unfit, and ben Beteira deems it fit.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:22:1.hebrew: אבל בשלא לשמו מודה רבי יהושע - דאע"ג דשחרית לאו זימניה הוא, פסול, הואיל ומקצתו של יום ראוי לשמו. קמ"ל:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:22:1.english: But [in a case of] not for its own sake, Rabbi Yehoshua concedes - For even though the morning is not its [proper] time, [the offering] is disqualified, since part of the day is fit for its [designated] purpose. [The mishna] therefore teaches us [that they disagree even here].

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:23:1.hebrew: והא כתיב בין הערבים - לרבי אושעיא פריך, היכי מצי למימר פסח זמנו שחרית:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:23:1.english: But isn't it written, "between the evenings" - [The Gemara] asks against Rabbi Oshaya: How can he say that the time of the Paschal offering is in the morning?

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:24:1.hebrew: בין שני ערבים - מעלות השחר עד שקיעת החמה, דהיינו בין סוף ערב דאתמול ותחילת ערב דאורתא:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:24:1.english: Between two evenings - From dawn until sunset, which is between the end of yesterday's evening and the beginning of tomorrow's evening.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:27:1.hebrew: ואימא חד בבקר - את הראשון לא ישהא יותר מחצות, והשני כל היום זמנו, רצה שחרית רצה ערבית, כדכתיב ״בין הערבים״ ואתה דמפרשת ליה כל יומא:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:27:1.english: And say: one in the morning - The first one he should not delay beyond midday, and the second one, its time is all day long — whether in the morning or in the evening — as it is written "between the evenings," which you interpret as meaning the whole day.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:28:1.hebrew: ולא שנים בבקר - הלכך, על כרחך צריך להשהות את השני עד הערב:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:28:1.english: And not two in the morning - Therefore, you must perforce delay the second one until the evening.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:2:1.hebrew: ומה חטאת שמותרה כו' - ואם ק"ו כזה אתה דורש, יש לך לפסול עולה לשם חטאת. ומהכא דייק רבה מילתיה לעיל, מדלא אהדר ליה רבי אליעזר: אנא נמי פסילנא בנשחטין לשם חטאת:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:2:1.english: "Just as a sin offering, whose leftover…" etc. - If you derive an a fortiori argument like this, you should [likewise] disqualify a burnt offering [slaughtered] for the sake of a sin offering. And from here Rabbah derived the point he made above — from the fact that Rabbi Eliezer did not reply to him, "I too disqualify [offerings] that are slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering."

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:30:1.hebrew: מדתה - חצי לוג לכל נר ונר. כך שיערו חכמים: לילי תקופת טבת שהם הארוכים ביותר, שלא תכבה כל הלילה. ובתמוז ובניסן ובתשרי, אם תדליק שליש היום בלבד — לא איכפת לן:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:30:1.english: Its measure - Half a log for each and every lamp. So the Sages estimated: [for] the nights of the Tevet solstice [which are the longest], so that it will not go out all night. But in Tammuz, Nisan, and Tishrei, if it burns [only] a third of the day, it does not matter to us.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:30:2.hebrew: אין לך עבודה - מעבודות שהן אמורות ביום, כגון עבודות הדם, וקמצו, וקטרת, שכשרין מהדלקת נרות ואילך, שזו מאוחרת לכולן:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:30:2.english: You have no rite - Among the rites that are stated to be performed by day, such as the rites of the blood, the removal of the handful (of a meal offering), and the incense, which are valid [only] up to the lighting of the lamps; for this [lighting] is later than all of them.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:3:1.hebrew: שכן כשרה לשמה כל השנה - לפיכך עולה הנשחטת לשם חטאת כשרה:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:3:1.english: For it is fit for its own sake all year - Therefore, a burnt offering that is slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering is fit.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:5:1.hebrew: ולא יחללו את קדשי - אין (כאן) חילול כשירימו אותם לשם גבוה מהם:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:5:1.english: “And they shall not profane the holy things of” - There is no profanation [i.e., disqualification] when they are set apart for the sake of [an offering] more elevated than they are:

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:6:1.hebrew: בעתידין לתרום - דהיינו טבל, דכתיב ״ירימו״ — דבר העתיד. ומסיים בהא בסנהדרין פרק אלו הן הנשרפין: גמר חילול מתרומה, דכתיב בה ״ומתו בו כי יחללוהו״:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:6:1.english: Those that are destined to be separated - That is, untithed produce, as it is written “they will set apart” — [referring to] a matter of the future. And the conclusion of this [matter] is in Sanhedrin, in the chapter “These are the ones who are burned”: [the Gemara there] derives [the law of] profanation from teruma, about which it is written, “and they shall die through it, if they profane it.”

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:7:1.hebrew: א"כ - דלכר"ש אחי עזריה לחודיה אתא, לכתוב "ולא יחללו אשר הורמו"! מ"ש לשון עתיד דנקט? ש"מ, למידרש ביה נמי הא:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:7:1.english: If so - [I.e.,] if the verse came only for [the ruling of] Rabbi Shimon, brother of Azarya, it should have written, "And they shall not profane that which has been set apart" (past tense). Why does it use the future tense? Conclude from it that this too is to be derived from it:

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:8:1.hebrew: בעי רבי זירא - לשום גבוה מהן, כשרים דקתני שמעון אחי עזריה "כשרין ואין מרצין", קאמר כת"ק, ולא פליג אלא בנמוך, דקאמר פסולים לגמרי:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:8:1.english: Rabbi Zeira raised a dilemma - Regarding [offerings sacrificed] for the sake of a higher [sanctity] than theirs: when [Shimon, brother of Azaria] teaches that they are "fit but do not propitiate," he is saying [the same] as the first Tanna, and disagrees only about the lower [case], where he says [the offerings] are entirely disqualified.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:8:2.hebrew: ובתרתי פליגי - לשם גבוה מכשיר לגמרי, ובנמוך פסיל לגמרי. ואילו רבנן בתרוייהו מכשירים, ואין מרצין קאמרי:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:8:2.english: And they disagree about two [matters] - [Shimon brother of Azaria holds that a sacrifice offered] for the sake of a higher [offering] is entirely valid, while [one offered] for the sake of a lower [offering] is entirely disqualified. Whereas the Rabbis say that in both cases they are valid, but they do not propitiate.

Rashi on Zevachim 11b:9:1.hebrew: ת"ש - מדקא מפרש מילתיה ונקיט בכור ומעשר דלא לרצויי אתו, ש"מ שהשלמים כשרין ואינן מרצין קאמר:
Rashi on Zevachim 11b:9:1.english: Come and hear - Since he is explaining his statement, and mentions a firstborn and a tithe, which do not come to atone [i.e., to satisfy the owners' obligation], learn from this that he is saying that [peace offerings slaughtered for their sake] are fit, but they do not satisfy the owners' obligation:

Steinsaltz In-Depth comment #1 on Zevach.english: According to the first _tanna_, any offering that is sacrificed for the sake of another type of offering is fit but does not fulfill its owner’s obligation. Shimon, brother of Azarya, maintains, according to this suggestion, that an offering that is sacrificed for the sake of an offering of greater sanctity than it is fit and fulfills its owner's obligation, whereas an offering that is sacrificed for the sake of an offering of lesser sanctity than it is disqualified (Rashi). It might seem that he could have asked in another way: Perhaps Shimon, brother of Azarya, does not disagree about offerings sacrificed for the sake of less sacred ones, and when he said they are unfit, he only meant that they do not fulfill the owner's obligation, as we found this phrasing used elsewhere. However, it can be said that from the phrase “and they shall not profane,” which is the source for Rabbi Shimon ben Azarya’s statement (see above), it is clear that there is indeed profanation when one sacrifices for the sake of offerings of lesser sanctity (Shita Mekubbetzet, and similarly in Tosafot above on 4b).

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 11b:8.english: ב Rabbi Zeira asks: Is the intention of Shimon, brother of Azarya, that if one slaughtered them for the sake of offerings of greater sanctity than theirs, they are fit but do not fulfill the owner's obligation to God, as is the opinion of the Rabbis in the mishna? And if so, when Shimon, brother of Azarya, disagrees with the Rabbis, he disagrees about only one matter, namely, regarding those offerings slaughtered for the sake of offerings of lesser sanctity, which in his opinion are completely unfit. Or perhaps his intention is that offerings slaughtered for the sake of offerings of greater sanctity are both fit and fulfill the owner's obligation, and according to this, he disagrees about two matters. For in the opinion of the Rabbis, if one slaughtered them for the sake of offerings of greater sanctity, they are fit, but they do not fulfill the owner's obligation.

Tosafot on Zevachim 11b:21:1.hebrew: הג"ה אי איפלוג בלשמן כו' - ותימה: השתא נמי דפליגי בשלא לשמן, אני יכול לטעות כר"י לבן בתירא שיפסול י"ד לשמו שחרית, ולפרש טעמו משום דמקצתו ראוי. וי"ל דמזה אינו חושש, משום דשום תנא לא מכשיר פסח שחרית אלא זה:
Tosafot on Zevachim 11b:21:1.english: Gloss: "If so, let them disagree about [a Paschal offering slaughtered] for its sake," etc. - This is puzzling: Even now that they disagree about [a Paschal offering slaughtered] not for its sake, I could err like Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira, who disqualifies [a Paschal offering slaughtered] on the fourteenth in the morning for its sake, and explain his reason as being that part of it [i.e., part of the day] is fit. And one can answer that he is not concerned about this, because no other Tanna deems a Paschal offering fit in the morning except this one:

Tosafot on Zevachim 11b:28:1.hebrew: הג"ה (הגהה): אחד בבקר ולא שנים בבקר - בעלמא דרשינן "אחד" – מן המיוחד שבעדרו (מגילה דף כח.):
Tosafot on Zevachim 11b:28:1.english: Gloss: "One in the morning, and not two in the morning" - Elsewhere we derive from "one" [that it means] the choicest one in one's flock (Megillah 28a):

Tosafot on Zevachim 11b:3:1.hebrew: אמר ר' אליעזר לא אם אמרת בחטאת - דין הוא שאחרים כשרים לשמו. [וקשה], נהי דלא דמי לפסח, מ"מ ק"ו איכא; וא"כ [תימא] יפסלו נמי מהאי דינא: מותר חטאת בא עולה, כמו דינא דמותר פסח בא שלמים. וי"ל דאעיקר טעמו סמיך, כדאיתא בפסחים (דף סב:). וצ"ל דהא "לא אם אמרת" דקאמר רבי אליעזר, לדברי רבי יהושע קאמר, אליבא דרבי יוחנן. ורבינו תם מצא בספר ישן ברישא דשמעתא: "רבה אמר באחרים לשם חטאת", ומצא "ובאחרים" בוי"ו; ורבה לא בא אלא לפרש דברי רבי יוחנן, ור' יוחנן עצמו מודה דבאחרים לשם חטאת פליגי, ולא אמר "אמרו דבר אחד" אלא באחרים לשם פסח:
Tosafot on Zevachim 11b:3:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer said: "No, if you said regarding a sin offering" - It is logical that other offerings sacrificed for its sake are fit. [This is difficult]: Granted, it is not comparable to the Paschal offering, but nevertheless there is an a fortiori argument here! And if so, [one would have to say] that they should also be disqualified by this same reasoning: the surplus of a sin offering that is brought as a burnt offering, just like the ruling of the surplus of a Paschal offering that is brought as a peace offering. And one can answer that he relies on its fundamental reasoning, as stated in Pesachim (62b). And one must say that this "No, if you said" that Rabbi Eliezer states, he says according to the view of Rabbi Yehoshua, in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan. And Rabbeinu Tam found in an old book at the beginning of the passage: "Rabbah said: regarding other offerings for the sake of a sin offering," and he found "and regarding other offerings" with a vav; and Rabbah came only to explain the words of Rabbi Yochanan, and Rabbi Yochanan himself agrees that they disagree regarding other offerings for the sake of a sin offering, and he said "they said one thing" only regarding other offerings for the sake of a Paschal offering:

Zevachim 11a:20.english: The mishna teaches: Yosef ben Ḥoni says: Other offerings that are slaughtered for the sake of a Pesach offering or a ḥatat offering are unfit. Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Yosef ben Ḥoni and Rabbi Eliezer said the same thing, i.e., Rabbi Eliezer agrees with Yosef ben Ḥoni.

Zevachim 11b:16.english: MISHNA: With regard to the Paschal offering that one slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth of Nisan, the day when the Paschal offering should be slaughtered in the afternoon, if he did so not for its sake, Rabbi Yehoshua deems it fit as though it were slaughtered on the thirteenth of Nisan. Ben Beteira deems it unfit as though it were slaughtered in the afternoon of the fourteenth.

Zevachim 11b:18.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Elazar says that Rabbi Oshaya says: Just as ben Beteira disqualifies a Paschal offering that one slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth of Nisan not for its sake, so too, ben Beteira would deem fit a Paschal offering that one slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth of Nisan for its sake, as he held that the entire day, the fourteenth of Nisan, is its designated time.

Zevachim 11b:8.english: Rabbi Zeira raises a dilemma: According to Shimon, brother of Azarya, who says that less sacred offerings sacrificed for the sake of more sacred offerings are fit, perhaps they are fit but do not fulfill the owner's obligation to God, as the Rabbis hold. If so, when Shimon, brother of Azarya, disagrees with the first _tanna_ in the mishna, he disagrees only with regard to one matter, i.e., that more sacred offerings sacrificed for the sake of less sacred ones are disqualified altogether. Alternatively, perhaps Shimon, brother of Azarya, holds that if less sacred offerings are sacrificed for the sake of more sacred offerings, they are both fit and fulfill the owner's obligation, and he disagrees with the Rabbis about two matters.
